paper_assessment.supporting_quote: This randomized clinical trial was conducted at an academic research institution between May 2014 and October 2015 as part of the National Institute of Mental Health-funded Fast-Fail Trial for Psychotic Spectrum Disorders project. ... INTERVENTIONS: Volunteers received either sequential ketamine (0.23 mg/kg infusion over 1 minute followed by 0.58 mg/kg/h infusion over 30 minutes and then 0.29 mg/kg/h infusion over 29 minutes) or placebo infusions. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Ketamine-induced changes in pharmacoBOLD, 1H MRS, and task-based fMRI measures, along with symptom ratings. ... As expected, large effect size and between-group differences were seen for all behavioral scales (Table 2 ).
paper_assessment.reasoning_summary: This is a randomized clinical trial investigating the effects of ketamine on imaging biomarkers and clinical symptom ratings in healthy volunteers. The paper reports original results on ketamine-induced changes in mood, psychotic, dissociative, and psychotomimetic symptoms, which are extracted as claims. The study is not treating a disorder but inducing symptoms in healthy individuals.
